IN THE HIGH COURT OF JUDICATURE AT BOMBAY
CRIMINAL APPELLATE JURISDICTION
Criminal Appeal No. 412 of 2016
State of Maharashtra v. Kumar
Decided on 12 March, 2019

[SYNTHETIC TEST FIXTURE — not a real judgment; written to exercise the annotation pipeline.]

1. This appeal is directed against the judgment of the Sessions Court convicting the appellant under S. 304A of the I.P.C. and sentencing him to rigorous imprisonment for two years.
2. The prosecution case is that on 14 March 2014 the appellant drove a truck rashly and
negligently on the highway and struck the deceased, who was riding a motorcycle.
3. An FIR was registered under Sections 279 and 304A of the Indian Penal Code, and after investigation a charge-sheet was filed against the accused.
4. Learned counsel for the appellant, Smt. R. Rao, contended that the deceased suddenly swerved into the path of the truck. It was further submitted that PW.2 was not a reliable witness.
5. The learned APP for the State argued that the eyewitness account is consistent with the medical evidence.
6. Section 304A punishes whoever causes the death of any person by doing any rash or negligent act not amounting to culpable homicide.
7. In State v. Kumar, this Court held that mere speed by itself does not establish rashness.
8. We find that the evidence of PW.2 is corroborated by the spot panchanama and the post-mortem report. The prosecution has proved that the appellant was driving rashly.
9. The appeal is accordingly dismissed, and the conviction and sentence of the appellant are confirmed.
